page: Microsoft Azure FX8-4mds_v2 is a constrained-core virtual machine positioned within Azure's compute-optimized FXmdsv2 series, characterized by an exceptionally high memory-to-vCPU allocation. The instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hyper-Threading is enabled with 2 threads per core, backed by 260 MB of L3 cache and support for modern instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions. It carries 168.0 GB of system memory (42.0 GB per vCPU) and includes a bundled 472 GB local NVMe SSD. It features no GPU acceleration.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate standout single-threaded performance coupled with typical throughput constraints of a 4-vCPU footprint. In Geekbench testing, the 4.2 GHz clock rate pushes single-core scores to 2,355.0 points (top 10%), alongside strong results in single-threaded gzip compression (34.91 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.41 GB/sec). However, multi-core scaling is bounded by the small core count; stress-ng multi-core execution (4,441.77) and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall into the bottom 25%. Potentially uncached memory bandwidth registers at 36.17 GB/sec for reads and 25.69 GB/sec for writes, both ranking in the lower quartile.

In terms of cost efficiency, the FX8-4mds_v2 offers high memory density per core without requiring the provisioning of higher core counts. This design proves beneficial for software licensed per core that necessitates vast RAM arrays. Conversely, workloads reliant heavily on parallel thread throughput or continuous memory bandwidth will find the resource profile unbalanced. The bundled high-speed NVMe storage provides low-latency local disk caching.

Given its high clock frequencies, vast memory allocation, and modest vCPU count, the FX8-4mds_v2 is well structured for per-core licensed in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA), caching systems like Redis (which reached 6.31 million SET operations/sec), and memory-intensive single-threaded data manipulation tasks.
